core_obligations: Injectivity (proof lines 5041-5044): there is a canonical map Gamma(S, F) -> Gamma(T, f_{small}^{-1}F), and it is injective because f is surjective, which follows since its geometric fibres are connected and hence nonempty.

Reduce surjectivity to a descent statement (proof lines 5047-5054): for a section alpha over T, since {T -> S} is an fpqc covering the cited description of pullbacks shows it suffices to prove that alpha pulls back to the same section over T x_S T by the two projections, and it suffices to check this on each geometric fibre (T x_S T)_{sbar}.

Compute on a geometric fibre (proof lines 5055-5069): over a geometric point sbar the fibre product is T_{sbar} x_{sbar} T_{sbar}, the restriction of F to T_{sbar} is constant with value F_{sbar}, and since T_{sbar} is connected every section of a constant sheaf is constant, so alpha|_{T_{sbar}} corresponds to an element of F_{sbar} and both pullbacks agree with it.
proof_roadmap: Build the canonical map and note injectivity from surjectivity of f.
Use the fpqc description of pullbacks to reduce surjectivity to equality of the two pullbacks to T x_S T.
Check that equality on each geometric fibre of T x_S T.
On such a fibre the sheaf is constant and the fibre is connected, so sections are constant, which forces the two pullbacks to agree.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a flat quasi-compact morphism f : T -> S whose geometric fibres are connected, sections of an abelian sheaf on S_etale agree with sections of its inverse image over T (statement lines 5029-5038). The proof has three distinct parts: injectivity from surjectivity of f, a reduction of surjectivity to the equality of the two pullbacks to T x_S T via the fpqc description of pullbacks (proof lines 5047-5054), and the crux, the computation on a single geometric fibre where the restriction of F is a constant sheaf on the connected scheme T_{sbar}, so that every section is constant and both pullbacks correspond to the same element of F_{sbar} (proof lines 5055-5069). The non-formal content is this connectedness argument. The claim is H2: one descent reduction plus one geometric-fibre computation.
